document.title: Executive Order 13129, Blocking Property and Prohibiting Transactions With the Taliban
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Terrorism and U.S. Policy
document.note: [Unclassified] Blocks assets and transactions connected to the Taliban, which controlled most of Afghanistan. It notes the Taliban provides safe haven to Usama bin Ladin and Al-Qaida, who have committed and threaten acts of violence against the U.S., and declares this an extraordinary threat to U.S. national security. Federal Register Vol. 64, No. 129.

key_claims: The Taliban allowed territory under its control in Afghanistan to serve as a safe haven and base of operations for Usama bin Ladin and Al-Qaida.
The US declared a national emergency treating Taliban policies as an extraordinary threat to national security and foreign policy.
Taliban property and that of persons acting for or supporting it was blocked, and US transactions with Taliban-held territory were prohibited.
The order defines the Taliban as the Kandahar-headquartered political/military entity with de facto control over the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.
Mohammed Omar, styled Amir al-Mumineen, is the only Taliban leader named in the Annex.
Commercial sales of agricultural goods and medicine to Taliban-held areas were to be authorized with safeguards against diversion.
